question: What is the primary purpose of teaching and learning theories in nursing education?

options.A: To provide a strict set of hospital administrative rules
options.B: To dictate the exact salary scale of nurse educators
options.C: To replace practical ward experience with classroom reading
options.D: To guide educators in designing effective curricula and clinical instruction

explanation: Theories provide structured frameworks that help educators plan how students acquire knowledge and clinical skills. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h1)

question: Why should a nurse educator understand multiple learning theories instead of relying on just one?

options.A: Single theories are completely outdated and legally banned from schools
options.B: Different clinical situations and students require diverse teaching approaches
options.C: Hospital accreditation bodies legally mandate the use of all known theories
options.D: Students perform better when confused by changing teaching styles daily

explanation: No single theory fits every learning scenario, so educators must select the best model for the context. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h1)

question: Behaviorism defines learning primarily through which of the following indicators?

options.C: Observable changes in external student behavior

explanation: Behaviorism concerns itself strictly with actions that can be seen and measured objectively. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h2)

question: A clinical instructor praises a student immediately after a successful sterile dressing change. Which behaviorist concept does this demonstrate?
explanation: Giving praise after an action adds a rewarding stimulus to encourage the repetition of that correct behavior. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h2)

question: How does cognitivism view the human mind during the learning process?

options.A: A passive receiver of external punishments
options.B: A rigid computer that cannot adapt to change
options.C: A blank slate shaped entirely by reflexes
options.D: An active processor of incoming information

explanation: Cognitivism focuses on internal mental operations such as thinking, memory organization, and problem-solving. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h3)

question: Why do nurse educators use concept maps based on cognitive learning theory?

options.A: To measure the physical speed at which a student writes notes
options.B: To help students organize and link new clinical data into existing mental schemas
options.C: To punish students who fail to memorize textbook definitions word for word
options.D: To replace actual bedside patient interaction with colorful drawings

explanation: Concept maps visually structure information, making it easier for working memory to encode and store in long-term memory. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h3)

question: According to constructivist theory, how do students acquire new knowledge?

options.A: By receiving direct rewards for changing observable physical habits
options.B: By actively building understandings from personal experiences and interactions
options.C: By passively listening to long lectures without asking questions
options.D: By memorizing isolated facts to repeat during written examinations

explanation: Constructivism views learning as an active process where learners construct meaning from what they do and experience. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h4)

question: A clinical preceptor guides a student through a difficult IV cannulation, slowly letting the student take full control. Which concept does this represent?
explanation: Temporary structural support that is gradually removed as competence increases is known as educational scaffolding. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of humanistic learning theory in education?

options.A: The whole person, including emotions, personal growth, and self-actualization
options.B: The computer-like processing speed of short-term working memory
options.C: The mechanical repetition of clinical checklists and exam scripts
options.D: The strict measurement of external reflexes and physical behaviors

explanation: Humanism centers on affective development, emotional safety, and the personal agency of the learner. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h5)

question: How does a humanistic teaching approach directly influence future nursing practice?

options.A: It forces students to memorize complex drug dosage calculations
options.B: It ensures students pass standardized multiple-choice board exams
options.C: It eliminates the need for clinical supervision in the hospital
options.D: It encourages students to show empathy and respect toward patients

explanation: Experiencing supportive, patient-centered teaching helps students model those same therapeutic attitudes with patients. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h5)

question: What is the term specifically used to describe the art and science of adult learning?
explanation: Andragogy focuses on the unique characteristics and needs of adult learners as distinct from children. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h6)

question: Why must nurse educators incorporate the prior life and work experiences of adult students?

options.A: Hospital regulations legally require instructors to review past employment
options.B: Prior experience replaces the need for textbook reading and laboratory work
options.C: Adults value their background and use it as a foundation for new knowledge
options.D: Students will fail exams if they do not talk about their personal history

explanation: Adult learners possess a rich reservoir of experience that serves as a valuable resource for group learning. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h6)

question: Social Learning Theory emphasizes that students acquire professional behaviors primarily through which method?

options.A: Memorizing abstract textbook definitions in isolation
options.B: Receiving direct physical punishment for incorrect clinical answers
options.C: Observing and imitating role models in a social environment
options.D: Discovering knowledge entirely on their own without mentors

explanation: Bandura showed that human beings learn a great deal simply by watching and modeling the actions of others. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h7)

question: Why is the behavior of clinical ward staff critical according to Social Learning Theory?

options.A: Students readily imitate both good and bad professional practices they observe
options.B: Hospital management penalizes wards where students ask too many questions
options.C: Observing staff replaces the need for formal classroom lectures entirely
options.D: Staff members grade the final written board examinations for students

explanation: Because students learn through role modeling, the everyday actions of clinical staff directly shape student professional conduct. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h7)

question: How should a nurse educator select which learning theory to apply in a specific lesson?

options.A: Pick whichever theory requires the least amount of preparation time
options.B: Follow strict government laws that mandate one theory per academic year
options.C: Match the theory to the learning objective, student level, and clinical context
options.D: Use the exact same behaviorist theory for every single class and lab session

explanation: Effective teaching requires flexibility, choosing the pedagogical framework that best fits the specific learning goal. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h8)

question: An instructor uses a behaviorist checklist for a skill test, then a humanistic debriefing after a stressful code. What does this practice demonstrate?

options.A: An illegal violation of standard educational accreditation guidelines
options.B: Blending multiple learning theories to suit different educational goals
options.C: A complete lack of consistency in teaching philosophy and assessment
options.D: The replacement of clinical practice with purely theoretical concepts

explanation: Different aspects of nursing education benefit from different theoretical models depending on the immediate objective. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h8)
